overview: The router owns committed URL state and SSRs the initial page for discovery. Client transitions cancel superseded requests and commit only a result matching the canonical query key. Reserve image dimensions and prioritize above-fold assets. The graph separates browser interaction state, server query state and the existing backend. It is one defensible approach; equivalent boundaries and well-argued alternatives are welcome.
limitations: Design checks inspect structure and written evidence only; they do not execute a UI or prove accessibility/performance.

estimation.assumption: 40 products with 100 KB thumbnails vs 20 KB responsive thumbnails
estimation.calculation: 40 × 100 KB = 4 MB; 40 × 20 KB = 800 KB before lazy-loading
estimation.result: Image sizing dominates an illustrative listing payload
estimation.implication: Measure actual encoded sizes, LCP, layout shifts and hydration; image budgets depend on device width.

components.purpose: Keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive-technology entry point. Client architecture only; backend internals are external dependencies.
components.rationale: Own this responsibility at the Browser / User boundary; keep communication explicit through the diagrammed dependency.

components.purpose: The router owns committed URL state and SSRs the initial page for discovery. Client transitions cancel superseded requests and commit only a result matching the canonical query key. Reserve image dimensions and prioritize above-fold assets. Performance plan: 40 products per page on a mobile network; prioritize one initial route and visible images, defer optional recommendation code. Accessibility: Label filter groups, expose selected filters and clear-all, announce result count without stealing focus; use semantic product links and accessible mobile filter dialog focus restoration. Failure recovery: Abort and key-check responses; keep the previous grid visibly marked as updating. Back/forward restores the same committed URL state. Trade-off: CSR can be enough for an internal authenticated catalog. SSR improves initial discoverability but adds hydration and personalized-cache boundaries.

failureCases.scenario: Route or identity changes while work is in flight
failureCases.handling: Dispose subscriptions, abort obsolete reads and ignore old generations; partition/clear private cache before showing a new account. Preserve only explicitly safe drafts.
